notes.heading: Semantic HTML Structure
notes.overview: Learn to structure web pages using modern HTML5 tags like header, nav, main, article, and footer.
notes.codeExplanation: Demonstrates clean, accessible page layout without generic div elements.
commonMistakes: Using `<div>` tags for everything instead of semantic tags
notes.cheatsheetSummary: Semantic markup gives meaning to Web content for search engines and screen readers.

flashcards.question: What is semantic HTML?
flashcards.answer: HTML elements that describe their meaning to both developer and browser.

interviewQuestions.question: Why is semantic HTML important for SEO?
interviewQuestions.answer: Search engines use semantic structure to understand page content importance and hierarchy.

tasks.title: Task 1: Article Layout
tasks.problemStatement: Wrap a blog title and paragraph inside an `<article>` tag.

notes.heading: HTML5 Forms & Inputs
notes.overview: Build accessible forms using native HTML5 input types and client-side validation attributes.
notes.codeExplanation: Uses native browser email validation and accessible label coupling.
notes.expectedOutput: Form prevents submission if email format is invalid.
commonMistakes: Not associating `<label>` tags with inputs causing accessibility failures
notes.cheatsheetSummary: Native HTML5 form validation improves user experience without custom JavaScript.

flashcards.question: How do you bind a label to an input?
flashcards.answer: Match the label's `for` attribute value with the input's `id` attribute value.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the function of required attribute?
interviewQuestions.answer: It prevents form submission unless the corresponding input field is filled out.

tasks.title: Task 1: Email Input Field
tasks.problemStatement: Create a required email input field with label.

notes.heading: CSS Box Model Essentials
notes.overview: Master content, padding, border, and margin calculations alongside modern CSS selectors.
keyPoints: Understanding content, padding, border, and margin
notes.codeExplanation: Sets universal `border-box` sizing so padding doesn't expand total element width.
notes.expectedOutput: Card total width remains fixed at 300px.
notes.cheatsheetSummary: Border-box includes padding and border within an element's specified width.

flashcards.question: What is box-sizing: border-box?
flashcards.answer: A CSS property making width and height include content, padding, and border.

notes.heading: 1D Layouts with Flexbox
notes.overview: Align items along main and cross axes effortlessly using CSS Flexbox.
notes.codeExplanation: Distributes items evenly across main axis and aligns them vertically centered.
notes.expectedOutput: Flex items horizontally spaced and vertically aligned.
commonMistakes: Confusing main axis (`justify-content`) with cross axis (`align-items`)
notes.cheatsheetSummary: Flexbox excels at 1D alignment and dynamic spacing distribution.

interviewQuestions.question: How do you center an element vertically and horizontally with Flexbox?
interviewQuestions.answer: Set container to `display: flex; justify-content: center; align-items: center;`.

tasks.title: Task 1: Center Div
tasks.problemStatement: Center child div inside a full-screen parent container using flexbox.

modules.moduleTitle: Module 3: CSS Grid & Responsive Web Design

notes.heading: 2D Layouts with CSS Grid
notes.overview: Build complex 2D column and row layouts using modern CSS Grid specifications.
notes.codeExplanation: Creates a 3-column equal width grid layout with 20px spacing gaps.
commonMistakes: Using outdated float grids instead of native CSS Grid
notes.cheatsheetSummary: CSS Grid gives complete control over 2D web layout architectures.

flashcards.question: What is the `fr` unit in CSS Grid?
flashcards.answer: Fractional unit representing a fraction of available free space in grid container.

interviewQuestions.question: Difference between Flexbox and CSS Grid?
interviewQuestions.answer: Flexbox is designed for 1-dimensional layouts (row OR column), while CSS Grid handles 2-dimensional layouts (rows AND columns simultaneously).

tasks.title: Task 1: Equal 2-Column Grid
tasks.problemStatement: Create a 2-column grid container using fractional units.

notes.heading: Media Queries & Mobile-First Design
notes.overview: Adapt web design layouts fluidly across smartphones, tablets, and desktop displays.
notes.codeExplanation: Applies desktop container width constraints when screen size exceeds 768px width.
notes.expectedOutput: Layout adapts responsively based on viewport width.
commonMistakes: Missing `<meta name='viewport' content='width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0'>` tag in HTML
notes.cheatsheetSummary: Mobile-first design ensures optimal mobile experience by default, adding complex layouts via min-width queries.

flashcards.question: What is a breakpoint in CSS?
flashcards.answer: A screen width threshold where layout styles change via media query.

interviewQuestions.question: Why is viewport meta tag required for media queries?
interviewQuestions.answer: It tells mobile browsers to render page width matching physical screen width rather than desktop viewport emulation.

tasks.title: Task 1: Mobile-First Rule
tasks.problemStatement: Change font size to 18px on screens wider than 1024px.
